offence_severity: Life imprisonment (Section 302 read with Section 149 and 148 of IPC)
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the 'Dehati Nalishi' as the first information given to the police, but noted discrepancies in the identification of the accused by PW-5 and the absence of the appellants' names in the statement.
witness_credibility: The court expressed doubt about the credibility of PW-5's identification of the accused, noting that he did not name the three appellants in his statement and failed to identify them in court.

legal_representation.accused: U. R. Lalit, Sushil Kumar Jain, Meenakshi Arora, Sr. Advs. Puneet Jain, Harsh Jain, Abhinav Deshwal, Ms. Ankita Gupta, Shailendra Sharma (for Ms. Pratibha Jain), Ehtesham Hashmi, Akbar Siddique, Ms. Pallavi Pratap
legal_representation.state: Vaibhav Srivastava, DAG, Chandan Kumar, Pradyuman Kaistha (for Mrs. Swarupama Chaturvedi)

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeals allowed, convictions set aside, appellants acquitted

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the three appellants were present at the scene of the incident and were among the assailants who attacked and killed Babusingh. They claimed that the pillion riders informed Motisingh (PW-1) about the attack and that PW-5 identified four of the assailants, including the three appellants.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no evidence against the three appellants. The names of the appellants were absent in the 'Dehati Nalishi' and in PW-5's statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. The prosecution failed to provide a plausible explanation for the absence of the appellants' names, and PW-5 did not identify the appellants as the assailants in court.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle of the benefit of doubt in criminal cases, particularly when there is a grave doubt regarding the presence of the accused at the scene of the incident.
other_sentence_order: The appellants were acquitted and directed to be set free forthwith if not required in any other case. All pending applications were disposed of.
